J1.evidence: Verse 4206 تقولُ وقد دَرَأْتُ لها وَضِيْني: lexicographers (Lisan) explain دَرَأْتُ الوضين as spreading/pushing the girth toward the camel to fasten it. TR 'ona doğru çevirdiğimde' (turned it toward her) is an approximation of دَرَأ لها; whether acceptable needs a scholar's lexical judgement. Rest of TR is faithful.

J2.evidence: Verse 4206 «تقولُ وقد دَرَأْتُ لها وَضِيْني»: دَرَأَ الوضينَ (cf. Lisān al-ʿArab, citing this very verse of al-Muthaqqib) = to spread out / lay the girth (on the ground or her back) in order to fasten it, i.e. 'when I set/spread my girth for her'. TR «Kuşağımı ona doğru çevirdiğimde» ('turned toward her') does not render دَرَأْتُ; meaning is wrong and needs correction (e.g. 'kuşağımı onun için serip/yerleştirdiğimde').

J1.evidence: Verse 4206 تقولُ وقد دَرَأْتُ لها وَضِيْني: دَرَأَ = pushed/thrust (lexically: spread the girth toward the camel to fasten it); EN 'when I loosened my girth for her' gives a meaning not supported by دَرَأْتُ. Also EN quotes the root example as «وضَنْتُ الشيءَ» while the source reads وضَّنْتُ الشيءَ (shadda dropped), altering the Arabic quoted.

J2.evidence: Verse 4206 «تقولُ وقد دَرَأْتُ لها وَضِيْني»: دَرَأَ الوضينَ = to spread out/lay the girth in order to fasten it (Lisān al-ʿArab cites this verse), i.e. 'when I spread/set my girth for her'. EN 'when I loosened my girth for her' gives the opposite/wrong sense of دَرَأْتُ. Needs correction. (Also EN cites «وضَنْتُ» without the shadda the source has «وضَّنْتُ»; Arabic should be quoted as written.)

J1.evidence: Arabic: وقرأ ابنُ أبي عبلة «لا باردٌ ولا كريمٌ» برفعهما أي: هو لا باردٌ. TR renders the name as 'İbn Ebî Ablete' (wrong form of ابن أبي عبلة, standard 'İbn Ebî Able'), and also expands أي: هو لا باردٌ into 'o ne serindir ne cömerttir', adding the unmarked 'ne cömerttir' not in the Arabic (EN correctly has only 'it is not cool').

J2.evidence: Arabic «وقرأ ابنُ أبي عبلة»: the reader is Ibn Abī ʿAbla (عبلة). TR writes «İbn Ebî Ablete», adding a construct -te that does not belong to a name in this position; the established form, used about 102 times elsewhere in the TR files, is «İbn Ebî Able». A misspelled proper name of a qāriʾ; should be corrected to «İbn Ebî Able». Rest of the TR (two adjectives of ظل, يحموم, nominative reading, verse 4214) is accurate.
